letterText:
Alex Example
12 Sample Street
Exampletown
EX1 2MP

3 March 2026

Exampletown Borough Council
Parking Services – Appeals

Re: Penalty Charge Notice EX12345678
Vehicle registration: AB12 CDE · Date: 28 February 2026 · Location: Market Street car park

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to challenge the above Penalty Charge Notice, issued to my vehicle at Market Street car park on 28 February 2026. I respectfully ask that it is cancelled.

When I arrived, I attempted to pay at the only pay-and-display machine in the car park. The machine's screen was blank and it would not accept coins or cards. I could not see any notice on or near the machine explaining an alternative way to pay.

It is a reasonable expectation that a motorist who tries in good faith to pay, but is prevented from doing so by faulty equipment provided by the council, should not be penalised. I did not intend to park without paying and took a photograph of the blank machine at the time.

I would therefore be grateful if you would cancel this Penalty Charge Notice. If you need any further information, please contact me at the address above.

Yours faithfully,

Alex Example
evidence: If you have it: the photo of the blank payment machine, ideally showing the time and date.
If you have it: a photo of the car park signage near the machine.
If you have it: a bank statement showing no card payment was taken.
suggestions: Did you try any other machine or a phone payment option? If so, say which and what happened.
Note how long you were parked, if you know.
nextSteps: Check the deadline printed on your ticket. Councils often offer a reduced rate if you pay within a short period, and some will re-offer it if an early challenge is rejected.
Send this letter to the council as an informal challenge (or as formal representations if you have already received a Notice to Owner). Use their online form or postal address and keep a copy.
If the council rejects your formal representations, you can usually appeal to an independent parking adjudicator. The council’s rejection letter will explain how.
disclaimer: This is a letter-writing tool, not legal advice.
